### P34736 — Transketolase
- Organism: Scheffersomyces stipitis (strain ATCC 58785 / CBS 6054 / NBRC 10063 / NRRL Y-11545)
- Reviewed: True
- Source: local_uniprot_swissprot_xml
- Homology: identity=100.0%, query coverage=100.0%, target coverage=100.0%, E-value=0
- Exact reference sequence hash match: yes
- function: Catalyzes the transfer of a two-carbon ketol group from a ketose donor to an aldose acceptor, via a covalent intermediate with the cofactor thiamine pyrophosphate (PubMed:27578891). Thus, catalyzes the reversible transfer of a two-carbon ketol group from sedoheptulose-7-phosphate to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, producing xylulose-5-phosphate and ribose-5-phosphate (PubMed:27578891). The two-carbon ketol group is abstracted by thiamine pyrophosphate, probably via a diradical single electron transfer mechanism before being transferred to the aldose acceptor sugar (PubMed:30155962). Can utilize fructose-6-phosphate as a ketose donor and erythrose-4-phosphate as an aldose acceptor (PubMed:27578891).
- cofactor: Mg(2+); Ca(2+); Mn(2+); Co(2+); Binds 1 Mg(2+) ion per subunit. Can also utilize other divalent metal cations, such as Ca(2+), Mn(2+) and Co(2+) (By similarity) (PubMed:27578891, PubMed:29243887, PubMed:30155962).; ChEBI:CHEBI:18420; ChEBI:CHEBI:29108; ChEBI:CHEBI:29035; ChEBI:CHEBI:48828
- cofactor: thiamine diphosphate; Binds 1 thiamine pyrophosphate per subunit (PubMed:27578891, PubMed:29243887, PubMed:30155962). The thiazolium ring of thiamine pyrophosphate puckers when bound to the enzyme, with about 70% of the bound cofactor adopting a bent configuration and 30% planar (PubMed:29243887, PubMed:30155962).; ChEBI:CHEBI:58937
- pathway: Carbohydrate degradation; pentose phosphate pathway.
- subunit: Homodimer.
- EC: 2.2.1.1
